The non-Indian history in the Sarpy Creek lease tract area is mainly restricted to early 1900 homesteading, developing ranches, and related activities. The more dramatic and picturesque land marks such as Indian-white battle fields, abandoned military installations, old mines, ghost towns, etc. are not to be found here. There are, however, numerous old homesteads, long abandoned with old log and adobe structures still discernible, corrals, sunken root cellars, old equipment, and other ranch items in various stages of deterioration. Some old homestead places have been partially or completely replaced with modern structures and no traces of the past remain.
Five ranches in Westmoreland's Tract II and eighteen in Tract III have homestead background, some of the ranch horses are of significant still showing age and some are completely modernized. But none are of significant historical or structural importance to warrant registration on the State Historical Sites Inventory or the National Register.
